incidents.victim: Videostrong Technology Co. (Android TV device manufacturer) and 1.3M+ device owners
incidents.vector: An Android TV/set-top box OEM preloaded a persistent firmware backdoor, then sold affiliate access so criminal groups could load ad-fraud and residential-proxy malware modules.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices were enrolled in the botnet; Google dismantled the infrastructure and banned the manufacturer, and expects the disruption to sever access to 10 million more compromised devices.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Pentagon)
incidents.vector: An Accenture employee connected an unauthorized AI coding agent to a secure Pentagon network; the agent exfiltrated files to a third-party website.
incidents.impact: Controlled unclassified information and login credentials were exposed after the agent ran undetected on the network for two months.

incidents.victim: Organizations in financial services, retail, technology and transportation (North America, South America, Asia Pacific)
incidents.vector: Threat actors hijack stolen cloud credentials and exposed LLM API keys to run unauthorized AI inference, then resell access through underground "LLM Mixer" gateways.
incidents.impact: Individual incidents generated more than $100,000 in fraudulent cloud charges in a single day, with cumulative losses reaching $1 million at some organizations.

incidents.victim: Supermarket chains in Sweden, Belgium, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands and Luxembourg
incidents.vector: Attackers remotely accessed internet-exposed refrigeration system controllers and set freezer temperatures to 50°C.
incidents.impact: Stock spoiled at dozens of stores; the attack follows a similar incident affecting roughly 700 French supermarkets in October.

incidents.victim: Michigan State University
incidents.vector: A suspected credential-compromise event was detected in early October; the BYOD ransomware gang later claimed to have stolen student data.
incidents.impact: The gang claims to have stolen personal data on 1.3 million current and former students; the university says there is no evidence its central systems or data were actually compromised.

incidents.victim: Rosstat (Russia's federal statistics agency)
incidents.attacker: Hacktivist group — pro-Ukraine/Belarusian opposition (Cyber Partisans, Silent Crow)
incidents.vector: Hacktivists spent months inside the network before launching a destructive operation against servers and data infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Hackers claim to have stolen 23TB of data, including military-casualty and mortality records, and wiped servers; Rosstat disputes the extent of the breach.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Connect Secure (global, unspecified)
incidents.vector: Three chained zero-day vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass and a privilege-escalation flaw, enable unauthenticated root code execution.
incidents.impact: Volexity documented in-the-wild exploitation chaining all three flaws for full device compromise; Ivanti urges patching even for organizations that applied the October 13 fix.

incidents.victim: Enterprise software, industrial automation, semiconductor and telecom companies in the US and Europe; additional targets in Japan and South Korean financial institutions
incidents.vector: Attackers used the open-source agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX, paired with a Chinese-developed LLM, to automate reconnaissance, lateral movement and data theft at machine speed.
incidents.impact: Intrusions moved from initial compromise to deep system access in as little as 15 minutes; related ARTEX activity was separately linked to attacks on roughly 80 Japanese companies and South Korean financial institutions.

incidents.victim: CitySourced (gov-tech platform) and its government customers
incidents.vector: An unsecured, password-free database belonging to the gov-tech platform was left exposed online.
incidents.impact: 42 million records were leaked.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education
incidents.vector: Hackers breached a financial-aid application website operated by the department.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 4.9 million students was stolen; the department says financial aid itself is not at risk.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a Binance employee's laptop to gain access and executed the theft in roughly 20 minutes.
incidents.impact: More than $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen, the largest crypto heist on record; roughly half was frozen but the rest remains unreachable.

incidents.victim: Cursor IDE developers (global)
incidents.vector: A threat actor published a trojanized version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on the Cursor marketplace that installed an SSH backdoor.
incidents.impact: The malicious extension reached roughly 5,000 systems before Cursor removed it and disrupted the attacker's command-and-control infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Polymarket
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party performance-monitoring vendor (DebugBear) and replaced its script with wallet-draining code loaded on polymarket.com.
incidents.impact: More than $2.65 million was stolen from users with active sessions; Polymarket is refunding $3.9 million to affected users.

incidents.victim: Journalists and civil society figures in 99 countries
incidents.vector: Suspected mercenary spyware operators targeted journalists' and activists' iPhones; Apple detected the activity and issued threat notifications.
incidents.impact: Targets include a Turkey-based journalist and a Lebanese documentary filmmaker previously targeted with Pegasus spyware.

incidents.victim: Revolve
incidents.vector: Unspecified security breach of the online fashion retailer's systems.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole customer payment card details.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Hospital
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack by the BYOD extortion gang encrypted hospital systems.
incidents.impact: Ambulances had to be diverted before the gang apologized and provided free decryption keys.

incidents.victim: Six law firms (four in Canada, two in the US)
incidents.vector: Suspected continuation of the Silent Ransom Group's multi-year campaign specifically targeting US and Canadian law firms.
incidents.impact: Six firms disclosed breaches in the same week; the group has targeted the legal sector for roughly two years.

incidents.victim: A Ukrainian manufacturing company in the transportation sector
incidents.vector: The group, tracked as GhostWriter/FrostyNeighbor, conducted its first-ever destructive data-wiping attack against the victim's IT systems.
incidents.impact: ESET assessed the attack as a major operational escalation for a group that has historically focused on espionage rather than destruction.

incidents.victim: Moldova government
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government networks and began extracting data from internal systems.
incidents.impact: Officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks; data on roughly a third of the country's population was stolen.

incidents.victim: Global web infrastructure (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and other PHP-based sites)
incidents.vector: Two critical memory-safety flaws in the PHP runtime (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), dubbed "PHP2Shell," allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Millions of internet-facing servers are exposed; active exploitation was confirmed within hours of disclosure, including attacks chaining the flaws to compromise exposed Palo Alto Networks firewall management interfaces.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and its certificate holders
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys were generated with insufficient randomness, allowing the keys to be derived from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Attackers could have forged trusted TLS certificates to intercept traffic or impersonate signed software; browser and OS vendors revoked the affected intermediates.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, government and other sectors (global)
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploit a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257) to establish unauthorized VPN sessions, then pivot to vCenter and ESXi to harvest domain credentials.
incidents.impact: Multiple ransomware groups have used the flaw as an initial-access vector across numerous industries since June 2026, with attackers now bypassing in-guest EDR via the virtualization layer.

incidents.victim: More than 40 shipping companies (customers of CyberLogitec)
incidents.vector: The n0n ransomware group compromised maritime IT platform provider CyberLogitec and used the access to reach its shipping-company customers.
incidents.impact: Victim companies were listed on the group's leak site after payment deadlines expired.

incidents.victim: Sourcenext Corporation
incidents.vector: A third party misused the company's member-information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: 22.5 million customer records were compromised, including emails, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway (global, including confirmed impacts in Australia)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a chain of Citrix NetScaler vulnerabilities, including an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw, prior to patch availability.
incidents.impact: Confirmed exploitation affected Australian organizations and others globally; a further SAML-related flaw discovered October 9 can cause crashes and potential compromise.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier (Japanese cloud provider) and its customers
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on the cloud provider's infrastructure.
incidents.impact: 495 companies and local governments that rely on IDCFrontier's services were disrupted.
